Environment Canada (1997). Energy Related CO2 Emission Factors for Manufacturing Industries. Spreadsheet received from Ken Olsen, 28 November 1997; factors from "Trends in Canada's Greenhouse Gas Emissions (1990-1995)". One sheet, years 1995 and 1996.

EMISSION-FACTOR REFERENCE, SUPERSEDED - NO TECHNOLOGY DATA. A one-sheet spreadsheet (Sheet1; the other 15 sheets are empty) of energy-related CO2 emission factors for manufacturing industries, rows for 1996 and 1995 (identical except for small differences in heavy fuel oil and middle distillates). Values as printed: anthracite 2390 g/kg; U.S. bituminous 2495 g/kg; Canadian bituminous 2300 (NS), 2230 (NB), 2520 (QUE, ONT, MAN), 1700 (SASK, ALTA, BC) g/kg; sub-bituminous 1742; lignite 1520; coal coke 2480 g/kg; coke oven gas 1600 g/m3; petroleum coke 3502 g/kg; coke from catalytic cracker 3169 g/kg; refinery fuel gas 2000 g/L; heavy fuel oil 3090 g/L; middle distillates 2751 (1996) / 2749 (1995) g/L; propane 1530 g/L; natural gas 1880 g/m3. CO2 only; no CH4/N2O; no heating values or technology data. Superseded by the national factors in each later National Inventory Report, currently ECCC (2026) NIR 1990-2024 Annex 6 (eccc_2026_001), which gives marketable natural gas 1944 g/m3 for 2024 and 1899 g/m3 for 1990 (versus 1880 here), heavy fuel oil 3156 g/L and propane 1515 g/L. Unique content: none still useful; the province-grouped coal factors of 1995-96 are also in the VCR (2002) Section 9 factors file. Source of the numbers: "Trends in Canada's Greenhouse Gas Emissions (1990-1995)"; spreadsheet received by Ken Olsen 28 Nov 1997.
